//: Project-level MCP server configuration for Yama. Copy to .yama/mcp.json.
//trust: OFF BY DEFAULT. This file can launch arbitrary local commands with the process environment, and it lives in the reviewed checkout. Yama only loads it when YAMA_ENABLE_PROJECT_MCP=true is set from a TRUSTED context (set outside the checkout). Do not enable for untrusted forks/PRs.
//env: Use ${ENV_VAR} placeholders for secrets — they are substituted from the environment at load time and never committed.
//keys: Entries here merge OVER mcpServers.servers from the main config: a key with the same id (e.g. 'bitbucket'/'github') REPLACES that server's definition (pin a version, change its denylist, or disable it with enabled:false); any other key adds a custom server, exposed per its roles/modes. A CUSTOM server can expose any tool, so it is only as safe as what you configure — restrict it with blockedTools/allowedTools and trust it.
//passthrough: Definitions are forwarded to NeuroLink's addExternalMCPServer verbatim (after ${ENV} substitution), minus the Yama-routing keys enabled/roles/modes/allowedTools. Every NeuroLink server option works from here without a Yama change: transport stdio|http|sse|websocket, command/args/env, url/headers, timeout, retryConfig, auth (oauth2/bearer/api-key), httpOptions, rateLimiting, and any future option.

bitbucket.//: Optional override — pin the Bitbucket MCP server version without a code change. Pin an exact reviewed version, not @latest.

serena.//: Code-intelligence (LSP-backed) server — gives the reviewer cross-file symbol/reference knowledge beyond the diff. See Phase 4.
